svg.title: Four Gates Before a Cold Email Campaign Launches
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-cold-email-launch-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Four Gates Before a Cold Email Campaign Launches; subtitle: Domain isolation, warmup, list hygiene and seed testing; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is cold volume running only on lookalike secondary domains redirected to the main site?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stop. A main-email automation cost Ethan Fleming a $2,000-a-month client, and a 10,000-email blast tanked a client's main sending.; gate: G2; question: Are SPF, DKIM, DMARC and MX published and every inbox warmed 2 to 3 weeks?; pass next: G3; fail action: Keep warming. Smartlead keeps warmup running even after campaigns start.; gate: G3; question: Is the list 20% or less catch-all addresses?; pass next: G4; fail action: Trim catch-alls. MailReach sees around 23% of catch-alls bounce when sent all at once.; gate: G4; question: Do seed tests to Gmail and Outlook accounts you control land in the inbox?; pass next: Launch with bounce auto-pause armed at 5%; fail action: Do not launch harder. Stop and diagnose, per Coldbot.; caption: Practitioners treat authentication and warmup as prerequisites, then arm a 5% bounce auto-pause so a bad list cannot burn the fleet.; assumptions note: Gate order is an editorial sequence of the operator gates described. Coldbot stresses that passing them guarantees nothing about inbox placement.; note: Sources - Ethan Fleming Marketing (TB1PQrXx5s8 @ 00:08:53), Smartlead (GZEdhosrYRc @ 00:10:11 and 00:14:23), Damien - MailReach (8EaKo_iAiPE @ 00:07:24), Coldbot (fM-ywBq8yoU @ 00:05:21).

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Is cold volume running only on lookalike secondary domains redirected to the main site?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stop. A main-email automation cost Ethan Fleming a $2,000-a-month client, and a 10,000-email blast tanked a client's main sending.
gate: G2; question: Are SPF, DKIM, DMARC and MX published and every inbox warmed 2 to 3 weeks?; pass next: G3; fail action: Keep warming. Smartlead keeps warmup running even after campaigns start.
gate: G3; question: Is the list 20% or less catch-all addresses?; pass next: G4; fail action: Trim catch-alls. MailReach sees around 23% of catch-alls bounce when sent all at once.

gate: G4; question: Do seed tests to Gmail and Outlook accounts you control land in the inbox?; pass next: Launch with bounce auto-pause armed at 5%; fail action: Do not launch harder. Stop and diagnose, per Coldbot.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is an editorial sequence of the operator gates described. Coldbot stresses that passing them guarantees nothing about inbox placement.
